pagerbot: INCIDENT 2468001234 - GPU pool s-gpu-prod-3 sustained queue depth > 95% and autoscaler failed to add nodes, throttling observed across multiple models :rotating_light:
pagerbot: Alerting on-call (Ajay) and sending to #incidents
Ajay: ack, I'm on it. seeing large queue growth on s-gpu-prod-3, graphs show steady overflow for last 6m
Ajay: pulling logs now, likely related to v15 rollout (just shipped to hosted yesterday)
Sam: pinging infra-ops to confirm any node provisioning issues
infra-ops: noticed quota errors when provisioning gpus, vendor API returned 429s around 15:06 UTC
Maria: customers calling out 504s, CX reported spike from acme-inc and beta clients using the v15-chat endpoint
Claire: is this the context-size change from v15? that model bumped default context from 8k -> 32k
Ajay: yes, v15's tokenization change increases kv-layer state per request. combined with warmup traffic it's multiplying memory & p99 latency
Sam: current symptoms: queued requests rising, token-generation slow, autoscaler attempted 2 scale events but hit provisioning limit, then throttled requests at gateway
Ajay: runbook step 1: reduce ingress to affected model to limit tail-latency. applying traffic-shed via routing rules now
eng-release-bot: rollout v15 -> paused via canary flag by Maria at 15:12 UTC
Maria: done. paused rollout. sending note to releases and customers.
Ajay: runbook step 2: temporarily disable kv-prefetch for v15 to reduce per-request memory. I'm flipping the kv-prefetch flag on routing layer.
Sam: command I ran: ```curl -XPOST https://admin.internal/routing/flags -d '{"model":"v15","kv_prefetch":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'```
Ajay: applied. kv-prefetch off for v15. queue growth slowed but still high due to backlog
Claire: can we throttle heavy customers? which API keys are the top contributors?
Sam: top 5 API keys by token usage in last 30m: acme-inc-key, beta-test-2, internal-load-test, partner-x, dev-adhoc. acme-inc accounts for ~26% of requests to v15
Maria: contacting acme account team. advising to reduce test burst.
Ajay: runbook step 3: attempt manual scale: provisioning additional nodes in pool s-gpu-prod-3 but vendor quota is the blocker. infra-ops is requesting emergency quota increase with cloud provider
infra-ops: submitted ticket with priority, cloud says ~20-30m ETA on quota bump. also standing up a temporary spill pool s-gpu-burst in us-west using alternate vendor (if approved)
Sam: in parallel, enabling lower-memory fallback for v15: serve quantized v15-q8 for non-critical customers, config change pushed to routing at 15:21 UTC
Ajay: pushed fallback. traffic for anonymous/low-tier routes now diverted to v15-q8. observed immediate decrease in memory pressure on some nodes
Claire: output from the scaler logs around the failure: ```[15:09:12] autoscaler: scale attempt -> create-instances failed: rate limit exceeded (429)
[15:09:35] autoscaler: retrying (2)
[15:11:00] autoscaler: create-instances failed: quota exceeded (403)
[15:12:05] autoscaler: aborting further attempts, entering throttle-protect state```
Ajay: affected region: us-west-2. fallback routing directed ~40% traffic away, queue dropped from 1200 -> 230 in 25m
Maria: CX update drafted: "We detected elevated errors and latency impacting a subset of hosted API customers using the v15 model. We paused the rollout, enabled fallback model routing, and are working to restore full capacity. Some customers may have experienced request throttling or transient 5xx responses." sending to ops-cx now
Sam: monitoring metrics: p99 latency for text generation down from 6.3s -> 1.8s after mitigations, error rate still ~0.7% above baseline due to backlog processing
Claire: is there customer data at risk? logs show no data exfiltration, just service-level errors
Ajay: agree. no security flags. this is capacity/throughput only
infra-ops: cloud approved emergency pool in us-west (s-gpu-burst) but provisioning will take 12m. starting bootstrap now
Ajay: once burst pool up, we'll drain high-memory sessions there and scale down existing overloaded hosts
Maria: handoff to night on-call (Sam) at 16:00 UTC. I'll stay as incident lead for coordination and postmortem
Sam: ack, I'll take it. next steps for oncall: 1) validate burst pool health 2) verify backlog drains to <50 requests 3) coordinate final rollback vs staged resume with releases
eng-release-bot: note: v15 canary is paused. current commit revert requires releases approval
Ajay: quick mitigation note to include in postmortem: model v15 increased default seq_len because of tokenizer refactor -> multiplied kv state and warmup prefill traffic hit autoscaler assumptions. autoscaler lacked hard quota-aware backoff policy for vendor 429s
Claire: adding immediate action items: - add vendor-429-aware exponential backoff to autoscaler - add preflight for rollout that simulates kv-size distribution - add soft limit in router per-model to avoid single-model herd pressure
Maria: agreed. also action: notify top-10 customers by token usage and offer escalated support for any errors they saw
Sam: backlog now 120 -> 40 after burst pool nodes came up at 15:34 UTC; error rate falling to baseline by 15:45 UTC
Ajay: marking incident mitigated at 15:48 UTC, leaving it open for follow-up tasks
Maria: filing postmortem draft and will assign owners for infra, releases, and runtime.
Claire: notes to include in PM: exact mem per-request delta, kv-state growth factors, and a test harness to rehearse vendor rate-limit scenarios
Sam: will run a replay of production traffic on staging with v15 + kv-prefetch enabled to reproduce throughput regression, aim to complete by EOD
Ajay: closing updates: no data loss, limited customer 5xx/latency for ~45m, mitigation: paused rollout, disabled kv-prefetch, enabled quantized fallback, provisioned burst pool
pagerbot: INCIDENT 2468001234 status -> MITIGATED by team at 15:48 UTC. Please file postmortem in /incidents/postmortems and tag #eng-runtime #eng-infra #releases
Maria: thanks everyone. handing over to Sam for night watch.
Sam: thanks, I'll monitor overnight and pick up PM tasks tomorrow AM
